title: Console backend: enforce RBAC v2 on billing/org/SSO routes + integration tests
author: Chloe Martin
release_notes: Console backend now enforces RBAC v2 permissions on billing, org settings, and SSO configuration routes. Added integration coverage to prevent regressions and ensure each sensitive endpoint is guarded and emits consistent 403 reason codes.
commits: console-backend: add rbac v2 guard middleware for sensitive route groups
console-backend: map billing/org/sso handlers to explicit permissions
tests: add integration suite for deny/allow across default roles
tests: stabilize authz policy fixtures + helper for role assignment
docs(dev): add notes for running console authz integration tests locally
ci_checks: integration tests (console-backend): pass (rerun 1x after initial flake)
body: Summary: This PR wires RBAC v2 enforcement into the console backend for the highest-risk route groups (billing, org settings, SSO/SCIM configuration) and adds integration tests that assert allow/deny behavior for the default roles. This closes a gap where the console UI hid certain pages, but backend routes were still callable with a valid session token. Context: Part of ENG-5386 (Console RBAC v2) and depends on the shared authz library semantics from ENG-5384/ENG-5383. The goal here is consistent enforcement + auditability on sensitive administrative operations before we start broader rollout in Hosted and begin Private enablement docs. What changed (high level): (1) Added a small middleware (authzV2Guard) that constructs the RBAC v2 check inputs (resource/action/scope) for console requests and calls the shared evaluator. The middleware is used at the router level so we don’t rely on per-handler checks for these sensitive groups. (2) Implemented explicit permission mapping for routes under /billing/*, /org/settings/*, /sso/*, and /scim/* with one permission per sensitive operation. For now we intentionally avoid wildcard “admin:*” checks except for Org Admin to keep least-privilege roles meaningful. (3) Standardized deny responses to return 403 with consistent reason codes and logging fields (reason=RBAC_V2_DENY, permission, resource_id, actor_type, policy_version). This aligns with the ongoing authz error response work and makes it easier to correlate with audit log enrichment. (4) Added integration tests that spin up the console backend with a policy fixture and seeded org/project data, then assert allow/deny for Billing Admin vs Security Admin vs Org Admin vs Developer vs Read-only. Sensitive endpoints covered include: updating org name, managing verified domains, creating/updating SAML connections, rotating SCIM tokens, listing invoices, downloading invoice PDFs, and managing payment methods. Permissions added/used: org:update, org:read, org_domain:verify, billing_invoice:list, billing_invoice:download, billing_payment_method:read, billing_payment_method:update, sso_saml_connection:create, sso_saml_connection:update, sso_saml_connection:delete, sso_saml_connection:rotate_certificate, sso_domain:verify, scim_token:create, scim_token:revoke, scim_token:list. Notes on scope: This PR is console backend only. It does not add new UI gating (tracked separately) and does not change RBAC v1 behavior. These checks are evaluated only when RBAC v2 is enabled for the org via the existing feature flag (rbac_v2_console_enforce). In shadow mode we continue to evaluate and log but do not block; tests cover enforce mode only. Testing: Added test/integration/rbac_v2/* specs. These run in CI via the existing integration job. Locally: pnpm --filter console-backend test:integration -- rbac_v2. Rollout plan: Merge behind rbac_v2_console_enforce. We will enable for internal dogfood orgs first, then staged Hosted canary. If we see elevated 403s on these routes for customers (esp. Billing Admin and Security Admin splits), we can disable the flag per-org and continue investigating via logs (permission + decision fields). Reviewer focus: (a) Permission naming and mapping (ENG-5383 conventions). (b) Any route that should remain Org Admin only (esp. billing payment method updates and SSO/SCIM changes). (c) Test coverage for deny cases and stability of fixtures.
conversation: Marcus Lin (Security) — 2025-02-19: The set of routes looks right. Two asks: (1) please ensure billing invoice download is separate from invoice list/read; many customers want accounting to download but not change payment methods. (2) On SSO routes, make sure we don’t allow Developer to read SSO metadata (ACS URL, entity IDs) if it includes customer-specific identifiers; at minimum keep read behind Security Admin.

Chloe Martin (author) — 2025-02-19: Split download vs list is already separated (billing_invoice:list vs billing_invoice:download). For SSO reads: I currently allow Security Admin + Org Admin; Developer is deny. I’ll add explicit tests for the SSO GET endpoints to prevent accidental widening.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (Authz implementation) — 2025-02-20: Middleware approach is good. Can you ensure the guard always populates scope correctly? Specifically org-scoped routes should not accept an arbitrary orgId param if it doesn’t match session org. Also, please include permission + policy_version in structured logs (we use those fields in dashboards from ENG-5387).

Chloe Martin (author) — 2025-02-20: Good catch. I tightened the resolver so the orgId comes from the session context (and we compare if route contains orgId). Added structured fields: authz.permission, authz.policy_version, authz.decision, authz.reason. Pushed in 9f2b0b4.
Jada Williams (Console architecture) — 2025-02-21: Small nit: please avoid duplicating reason-code strings in handlers. We’ve had drift. Can we centralize constants?

Chloe Martin (author) — 2025-02-21: Done. Added util/authzReasonCodes.ts and migrated the handful of call sites that were setting a reason. The guard is now the only thing emitting RBAC v2 deny codes; handlers just throw Forbidden.

Leila Farouk (E2E test automation) — 2025-02-22: Integration tests are valuable but the server boot + policy fixture looks a bit heavy. I’m seeing a flaky failure in CI related to DB cleanup. Please add explicit cleanup in afterEach or use isolated schema per test run.

Chloe Martin (author) — 2025-02-22: Addressed by switching the helper to create a per-test org with randomized slug and ensuring token revocation happens in teardown. Also added retry on one known flaky invoice PDF stub call. CI rerun looks clean.

Tessa Morgan (Admin UX) — 2025-02-23: No UI changes here, but please confirm that the backend 403 returns a stable reason code we can map to a user-facing message (“You need Billing Admin to update payment methods”).

Chloe Martin (author) — 2025-02-23: Yep. 403 payload includes code=RBAC_FORBIDDEN and reason=RBAC_V2_DENY plus permission string. We can map permission -> UX copy on the frontend later; I added a short note in CHANGELOG for now.
Marcus Lin (Security) — 2025-02-24: Approving. Thanks for splitting billing permissions and adding the explicit SSO read tests.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (Authz implementation) — 2025-02-24: Approved. Scope handling looks correct now and logs align with our field names.
Leila Farouk (E2E test automation) — 2025-02-24: Approved after CI rerun.
